bark.note: stout yellow-green culms; pale straw nodes and sheaths

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: a stiff single shoot with flat, grey-green, sharply pointed leaves; it tillers and sends short rhizomes so each seedling becomes a round tussock widening up to 30 cm a year, and tussocks merge into a dense sward within one to two decades. Culms live about a year; old swards may die back after decades.
growth.source: IUCN GISD and NOBANIS fact sheets (seed viable only one season, 0.6-5% viable; tussock radial growth up to 30 cm/yr; flowers Jul-Oct, seed ripens in ~12 weeks; 0.3-1.3 m); Gray et al. 1991 ITE Spartina anglica research review (germination faster at 20 C, marsh die-back from the 1920s)

bark.note: woody rootstock; wiry green branched flowering stems

ground.silhouette: flat leaf rosette with a lilac spray

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings are small rosettes of oval, leathery, long-stalked leaves flat on the salt-marsh mud; the woody rootstock slowly branches into a clump of several rosettes. From about the second summer stiff, branched, flat-topped sprays of tiny lavender-purple flowers rise above the rosettes, turning upper marshes purple in July-August.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Limonium vulgare: clumping perennial of salt marshes and other maritime habitats, Atlantic Europe from SW Sweden to SW Iberia); timings and ages estimated.

leaf.note: leaves reduced to opposite fleshy scales fused around the jointed stem

bark.note: succulent jointed green stems; segments flush red in autumn

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling with 2 fleshy, finger-like green cotyledons, then a leafless, jointed, succulent green stem (the tiny leaves are fused into the segments) that branches into a little candelabra 10-30 cm tall. Flowers hide in the joints late in summer; the whole plant turns red or purple in autumn, sheds seed and dies.
growth.source: Davy, Bishop & Costa 2001, Biological Flora of the British Isles: Salicornia (spring germination on the marsh after rain lowers salinity, flowering Aug-Sep, seed shed in autumn, strictly annual); Wikipedia S. europaea (shoots harvested Jun-Aug, turns red/purple in autumn, edible)

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings are scarce in the marsh: two small fleshy cotyledons, then opposite, oval, silvery-grey mealy leaves. The young plant is a few low, rooting stems that spread by layering into a dense, silver-grey, knee-high mat lining creek banks and pool edges.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Halimione portulacoides, shrub to 1 m, flowers Jul-Sep, wind-pollinated); Useful Temperate Plants (to 0.75 m, seed ripe in autumn, germinates from winter on, salt-marsh creek edges); ScienceDirect 2006 on bracteoles and germination; growth and ages estimated.

fruiting.source: Wikipedia and Useful Temperate Plants (flowers Jul-Sep in short spikes, wind-pollinated, seed ripe in autumn); fruit a utricle in fused 3-lobed bracteoles 2.5-5 mm (standard floras), floats for water dispersal; fruit set and crop estimated.
